es.summary: Elevación de la temperatura central > 41 °C, generalmente por exposición al calor, infecciones o reacciones a anestésicos. Es una urgencia que requiere enfriamiento rápido.
key_points: Puede ser primaria (ej. hipertermia maligna) o secundaria (ej. golpe de calor)
Complicaciones incluyen daño cerebral, rabdomiolisis y falla renal
El enfriamiento rápido y la reposición de líquidos son esenciales

pathophysiology: El cuerpo supera la capacidad de disipar calor por sudoración y vasodilatación.
Aumento de la producción metabólica (ej. MH) eleva la temperatura interna.
Daño a proteínas y membranas celulares produce inflamación y disfunción orgánica.
risk_factors: Exposición prolongada a ambientes > 35 °C y alta humedad.
Infecciones febriles, especialmente en niños y ancianos.
Uso de anestésicos desencadenantes (halotano, sevoflurano) en MH.
signs_symptoms: Piel caliente, seca o sudorosa, enrojecida.
Taquicardia, hipotensión, confusión o pérdida de conciencia.
diagnostics: Temperatura central medida por termómetro rectal o timpánico.
CBC, CK (elevado en MH), electrolitos (Na+, K+), función renal (creatinina).
Gasometría arterial si hay alteración respiratoria.
treatment: Enfriamiento activo: compresas frías, baño de agua tibia, ventilación con aire frío.
Paracetamol o ibuprofeno para reducir fiebre secundaria.
Reposición de líquidos IV (solución cristaloide) y corrección de electrolitos.
complications: Golpe de calor con daño cerebral irreversible.
Coagulopatía por consumo de factores de coagulación.
nursing_care: Medir temperatura cada 5‑15 min y registrar tendencia.
Iniciar medidas de enfriamiento inmediato y monitorizar la respuesta.
Evaluar estado mental, pulso, presión arterial y saturación de O₂.
Administrar líquidos IV según orden y vigilar balance hídrico.
Observar signos de complicaciones: color de orina, dolor muscular, alteración del ritmo cardíaco.
patient_teaching: Beber al menos 2 L de agua al día y más si hay sudoración excesiva.
Evitar exposición directa al sol entre 10:00 y 16:00 h.
Usar ropa ligera, sombrero y protector solar.
Reconocer síntomas de sobrecalentamiento y buscar atención médica inmediata.

outcomes: Temperatura corporal dentro de rango normal (36.5‑37.5 °C) en 2 h
Piel fresca y húmeda en 30 min
Sin signos de daño neurológico al alta

en.summary: Central temperature elevation > 41 °C, usually due to heat exposure, infections or anesthetic reactions. It is an emergency requiring rapid cooling.
key_points: Can be primary (e.g., malignant hyperthermia) or secondary (e.g., heat stroke)
Complications include brain injury, rhabdomyolysis, and renal failure
Rapid cooling and fluid replacement are essential

pathophysiology: The body exceeds its ability to dissipate heat via sweating and vasodilation.
Increased metabolic production (e.g., MH) raises internal temperature.
Protein and cellular membrane damage causes inflammation and organ dysfunction.
risk_factors: Prolonged exposure to environments > 35 °C and high humidity.
Febrile infections, especially in children and the elderly.
Use of triggering anesthetics (halothane, sevoflurane) in MH.
signs_symptoms: Warm, dry or sweaty, reddened skin.
Tachycardia, hypotension, confusion or loss of consciousness.
diagnostics: Central temperature measured by rectal or tympanic thermometer.
CBC, CK (elevated in MH), electrolytes (Na⁺, K⁺), renal function (creatinine).
Arterial blood gas if respiratory alteration.
treatment: Active cooling: cold compresses, lukewarm bath, ventilation with cool air.
Paracetamol or ibuprofen to reduce secondary fever.
IV fluid replacement (crystalloid solution) and electrolyte correction.
complications: Heat stroke with irreversible brain damage.
Coagulopathy from consumption of clotting factors.
nursing_care: Measure temperature every 5‑15 min and record trend.
Initiate immediate cooling measures and monitor response.
Assess mental status, pulse, blood pressure, and O₂ saturation.
Administer IV fluids per order and monitor fluid balance.
Observe for complications: urine color, muscle pain, cardiac rhythm changes.
patient_teaching: Drink at least 2 L of water daily and more if excessive sweating.
Avoid direct sun exposure between 10:00 and 16:00 h.
Wear light clothing, hat, and sunscreen.
Recognize overheating symptoms and seek medical attention immediately.

outcomes: Body temperature within normal range (36.5‑37.5 °C) in 2 h
Skin cool and moist within 30 min
No signs of neurological damage at discharge

interventions.action: Measure rectal temperature every 5 min and record
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid detection of response to cooling

interventions.action: Apply cold compresses to neck, axillae, and groin
interventions.rationale: Facilitates heat loss by conduction

interventions.action: Initiate ventilation with cool air and supplemental oxygen if needed
interventions.rationale: Prevents hypoxia and aids in lowering core temperature

interventions.action: Administer IV dantrolene per protocol if malignant hyperthermia suspected
interventions.rationale: Blocks muscle calcium release and stops metabolic rise

interventions.action: Replace fluids with isotonic crystalloid solution and monitor fluid balance
interventions.rationale: Corrects dehydration and prevents hypotension

interventions.action: Assess CK and renal function every 6 h
interventions.rationale: Detects rhabdomyolysis and early renal injury

outcomes: Electrolytes (Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻) within normal ranges in 24 h
Adequate hydration evidenced by central venous pressure < 8 cm H₂O

interventions.action: Monitor serum electrolytes every 12 h
interventions.rationale: Identifies early changes and allows timely correction

interventions.action: Administer isotonic saline IV as needed
interventions.rationale: Replaces sodium and water losses

interventions.action: Offer oral electrolyte solutions when patient is alert
interventions.rationale: Maintains fluid and electrolyte balance

interventions.action: Assess signs of hyperkalemia or hypokalemia (arrhythmias, muscle weakness)
interventions.rationale: Prevents cardiac complications

interventions.action: Document fluid intake and output each shift
interventions.rationale: Facilitates fluid balance calculation

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of rehydration and recognizing cramps or palpitations
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑care and prevention of recurrences

key_points.0.quote: When the core body temperature is more than 105.8°F (41°C), hyperthermia occurs.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Other team members institute prompt cooling measures: administer cold IV fluids; pack the patient’s neck and head, groin, axilla, and any open cavities with ice; change the forced-air blanket to cool air; and provide supportive care, which is crucial for successful MH management.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Common antipyretics are acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) and ibuprofen .
